design_space.current_assumption: 128/384/512 with three convs per block is the right shape.
design_space.why_material: Capacity is the binding constraint (F-003); shape sets both accuracy per epoch and seconds per epoch.

alternatives: fractional epochs tuned to the target
design_space.why_material: Time is linear in epochs; the best P1 cell sits at the grid edge.

design_space.current_assumption: airbench SGD with lookahead and triangular schedule.
alternatives: Muon on filters with SGD on biases and head
design_space.why_material: Muon cut CIFAR-10 epochs by about 20%.
Larger batches raise GPU efficiency but may need more epochs.
Low-resolution epochs cost about 44% fewer FLOPs.
Short budgets on CIFAR-100 may want less regularisation.
Compile cut CIFAR-10 time 14% at unchanged accuracy; it changes time, not accuracy.

design_space.current_assumption: Every example and every layer receives a full forward and backward pass every step.
alternatives: freeze early stages late in training
train the main net only on the hardest examples of each batch
end training below the evaluation resolution
design_space.why_material: Backward passes through early high-resolution stages and easy examples consume much of the step cost while contributing little late in training.

hypotheses.proposition: The airbench96 shape reaches 75.3% below 10 epochs, or a nearby depth-3 shape reaches it at lower proxy time.
hypotheses.mechanism: Residual three-conv blocks raise accuracy per epoch enough that fewer epochs or fewer channels suffice.
hypotheses.prediction: Interpolated time to 75.3% below 9.3 s for some depth-3 shape.

hypotheses.proposition: Muon on conv filters reduces epochs to 75.3% by at least 10% at the selected shape.
hypotheses.mechanism: Orthogonalised updates equalise progress across filter directions.
hypotheses.prediction: Muon reaches the target in at least 10% fewer epochs at small Newton-Schulz overhead.
hypotheses.disconfirming_result: Proxy time at target within noise of SGD or worse.

hypotheses.proposition: Progressive resizing (24 or 24-28 px early, 32 px late) lowers proxy time by at least 5% at matched accuracy.
hypotheses.mechanism: Early epochs learn coarse features at lower resolution and lower cost.
hypotheses.prediction: Time at target at least 5% lower.
hypotheses.disconfirming_result: Accuracy loss costs more epochs than the cheaper epochs save.

hypotheses.proposition: A larger batch (1536 or 2048) lowers proxy time at matched accuracy through higher GPU efficiency.
hypotheses.mechanism: Fewer, larger steps use the GPU better; airbench's decoupled parametrisation keeps step sizes comparable.
hypotheses.prediction: Seconds per epoch fall more than epochs to target rise.
hypotheses.disconfirming_result: Epochs to target rise by more than the per-epoch saving.

hypotheses.proposition: Weaker regularisation (label smoothing 0.1, lookahead off) suits short wide runs.
hypotheses.mechanism: Short budgets underfit rather than overfit, so regularisation slows convergence.
hypotheses.prediction: Accuracy at fixed epochs rises at least 0.2 pp.

hypotheses.proposition: torch.compile lowers seconds per epoch by at least 10% at unchanged accuracy.
hypotheses.mechanism: Kernel fusion removes elementwise and launch overhead.
hypotheses.prediction: Compiled proxy time at least 10% lower with accuracy within noise.

hypotheses.proposition: Freezing the whitening layer and first stage (then the second) late in training lowers proxy time at matched accuracy.
hypotheses.mechanism: Early filters converge first, so dropping their backward pass late in training saves compute at little accuracy cost (FreezeOut).
hypotheses.prediction: Proxy time to 75.3% at least 5% lower.
hypotheses.disconfirming_result: Accuracy loss costs more epochs than the saved backward compute.
hypotheses.decision_changed: Whether the recipe uses a freeze schedule.

hypotheses.proposition: Ending training at 28 px and evaluating single-view at 32 px matches full-resolution endings at lower cost.
hypotheses.mechanism: Train-test resolution discrepancy: random-crop training makes objects look larger than at test, so a lower final training resolution can be neutral or helpful (FixRes).
hypotheses.prediction: Equal or higher accuracy at fixed epochs with cheaper late epochs.
hypotheses.disconfirming_result: Accuracy at fixed epochs falls by more than 0.3 pp.

hypotheses.proposition: Training the main net on the highest-loss half of each batch, scored by a small selector net, lowers proxy time.
hypotheses.mechanism: Easy examples contribute little gradient late in training; halving the main batch halves its cost while the selector is cheap.
hypotheses.prediction: Proxy time to 75.3% at least 5% lower despite more epochs.
hypotheses.disconfirming_result: Extra epochs needed exceed the per-epoch saving.
hypotheses.decision_changed: Whether the recipe uses in-run selection.

hypotheses.proposition: Compilation (fused kernels; CUDA graphs in max-autotune) with fused SGD lowers seconds per epoch at unchanged accuracy.
hypotheses.mechanism: Kernel fusion and graph replay remove elementwise and launch overhead that dominates small-batch steps.
hypotheses.prediction: At least 10% lower proxy time with accuracy within noise.
hypotheses.decision_changed: Whether timing runs compile and which mode.

hypotheses.proposition: A learning rate of 0.8x or 1.25x the airbench default suits the wide depth-3 resized base better.
hypotheses.mechanism: The default was tuned for airbench94 on CIFAR-10.
hypotheses.prediction: Accuracy at fixed epochs changes by more than 0.3 pp.
hypotheses.disconfirming_result: Both directions within noise or worse.

hypotheses.proposition: Pooling before the widening conv in stages 2-3 frees FLOPs that buy more accuracy as width.
hypotheses.mechanism: The widening conv at pre-pool resolution is about 40% of FLOPs.
hypotheses.prediction: Equal accuracy at lower proxy time.
hypotheses.disconfirming_result: Accuracy falls by more than the FLOP saving.

hypotheses.proposition: Last-stage width beyond 512 is the cheapest capacity.
hypotheses.mechanism: Late stages run at 4-8 px, so channels are cheap there and carry the 100-way discrimination.
hypotheses.prediction: Lower proxy time to target at 640-768 last-stage channels.

hypotheses.proposition: Index-free amax pooling removes the pooling backward cost.
hypotheses.mechanism: Reshape plus amax yields a fusable elementwise backward without atomics.

hypotheses.proposition: A sharper softmax (logit scale 1/6) speeds short-run convergence.
hypotheses.mechanism: With label smoothing 0.2 and a 1/9 scale the logits are too soft early; competitor evidence shows a 1.5x gain.
hypotheses.prediction: Accuracy at fixed epochs rises at least 0.2 pp.

observations.statement: P1: the airbench96 shape reaches 75.37% single-view at 10 epochs (9.3 s local proxy, the best cell, at the grid edge); 2x two-conv width crosses at 13.7 epochs (12.0 s); narrow nets plateau below 75% (F-003).

probes.method: Depth-3 sweep: 128/384/512 at 6-10 epochs, 96/256/384 and 128/512/768 at 6, 8, 10 epochs, translate 2 vs 4 at 8 and 10 epochs; 5 seeds each.
probes.decision_rule: Select the shape and translate setting with the lowest interpolated proxy time to 75.3%.
probes.information_gain: Fixes the base before lever comparisons, which are only meaningful at the right shape.

probes.method: At the S3 base, run each lever at two epoch counts bracketing the target with 5 seeds, and interpolate proxy time to 75.3%.
probes.decision_rule: Adopt a lever if its interpolated proxy time is at least 3% lower than the base and its accuracy gain at fixed epochs exceeds two standard errors.
probes.information_gain: One pass decides four levers at the regime that matters.

probes.method: Tune the resize schedule (fraction and stages) at the base and test the wide shape with resizing; 5 seeds per cell.
probes.decision_rule: Keep the lowest interpolated proxy time unless within the 5% noise band, then prefer the simplest schedule.
probes.information_gain: Settles the resolution lever before stacking other levers.

probes.method: At the S5 base, compare control, compile with fused SGD, two freeze schedules and two FixRes-style endings at 10 and 12 epochs, 5 seeds each.
probes.decision_rule: Adopt a lever if proxy time to 75.3% is at least 5% lower than the in-sweep control.
probes.information_gain: Tests one systems and two novel compute-allocation levers in one pass.

probes.method: At the S5 base, compare control, in-run selection (keep 50% or 70%), max-autotune compilation with fused SGD, and lr 9.2 or 14.4, at 10-14 epochs, 5 seeds each.
probes.decision_rule: Adopt a lever if proxy time to 75.3% is at least 5% lower than the in-sweep control.
probes.information_gain: Tests example selection, CUDA-graph compilation and the learning rate together.

probes.decision_rule: Adopt compile if faster at unchanged accuracy.

probes.decision_rule: Select the shortest budget meeting 75.2% over 40 fresh seeds; declare saturation if no lever beats control beyond noise.
probes.information_gain: Sets the final budget and tests the last plausible levers.

question: Which levers lower local proxy time to a 75.3% single-view mean from the airbench96-shape base, and when does the climb saturate?
synthesis: Converged recipe: 128/384/640 airbench96-style net (three convs per block with a residual), translate 2, alternating flip, label smoothing 0.2, logit scale 1/6, SGD with lookahead, batch 1024, 20 px then 32 px at half-way, compiled (dynamic=False) with fused SGD, 8.25 epochs: 75.26% over 40 fresh seeds (75.25% over 60) at 5.38 s local compiled proxy, down from 9.3 s for the P1 best cell. Rejected: Muon, in-run selection, freezing, FixRes endings, pool-first, amax pooling, batch-size, learning-rate and schedule changes. Further accessible probes cannot change the recipe beyond noise; the open questions are A100 timing and cross-stack accuracy transfer (T-004, T-015).
